account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: morning correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and tea at the east-bank dockside cottage. The treasury held 128 emeralds; I withdrew none, and the secretary said no account papers had arrived. At the market, several townsfolk repeated that the baker had carried a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with baking supplies; I have no evidence of anything unusual behind it.

The tea arrangements were oddly uncertain. The appointment book listed tea with the neighbour, but the secretary could not confirm either host or cottage beforehand, despite enquiries at cottages and among warehouse workers. We nevertheless found the neighbour waiting at the dockside cottage, where I arrived at about 15:12. The neighbour welcomed us and described a quiet afternoon. They requested an ordinary meeting at town hall tomorrow at 18:00, which I accepted and asked the secretary to record. No subject or preparation has been specified, so I do not yet know what the meeting is for.

The secretary has accompanied me and kept track of appointments. It is now just after 16:00, and I need to return to town hall for my 16:30 office appointment. Tomorrow also has a mill grain inspection and council letters scheduled, as well as another afternoon tea. Nothing I have heard establishes wrongdoing or a crisis.
